<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **10** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `@objectstack/service-realtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **40** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/object.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**24** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/object.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **184** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4ce76a40f9e97507ab508c6067eceaa34a5ccb7b` — the merge of head `aa362ba1a79d95585d2c189fc4197ba6293133c6` into base `9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4ce76a40f9e97507ab508c6067eceaa34a5ccb7b && git checkout 4ce76a40f9e97507ab508c6067eceaa34a5ccb7b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19 aa362ba1a79d95585d2c189fc4197ba6293133c6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19 && git merge --no-ff aa362ba1a79d95585d2c189fc4197ba6293133c6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9abc732132a2f723627d585b049e2cc10869db19` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

L1 REWORK · head `851997e677adc14a324b8634a1325e683d58b11a` · 2026-11-22T10:57Z

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化:记录「动态」里的每条修改,现在默认在服务端记下并提供「字段:旧值 → 新值」,所有对象都一样。对象写 `enable: { fieldHistory: false }` 可以整体关掉,字段写 `trackHistory: false` 可以单独关掉。密码、密钥类字段永远不记值;图片、文件、JSON 这类字段只有显式写 `trackHistory: true` 才记。成员只拿得到自己有权读取的字段的修改,`sys_audit_log` 不对成员开放。这是三个 PR 里的第 1 个(规格和服务端);逐字段显示和「修改历史」卡片在后两个 PR。
- 为什么做:卡 #36290「字段修改历史」,按席位批准的方案 B(新开关 `enable.fieldHistory`,不设默认值)执行。
- 出错会怎样:最坏情况是成员看到不该看到的字段旧值或新值(读取时已逐条收窄,有测试钉住);或者动态写入失败(摘要已按 500 字符截断)。可以整体撤回,已写入的动态不受影响。
- 升级注意:单写 `enable.trackHistory: false` 不再能关掉值的显示,要关请改写 `enable.fieldHistory: false`;仓库里 44 个平台对象已经补上,HotCRM 没有对象需要改。
- 要你做什么:无。
- 席位意见:REWORK,只有一项:`Skills-docs:` 那一行欠的卡还没立。实现和测试我读下来是对的,见下面。

## 要改的(1 项)

1. **`Skills-docs: follow-up owed` 要先立卡,再把这一行改成 `Skills-docs: carried by #N`。** L1 清单的规定是:写 `follow-up owed` 的,要在 ACCEPT 之前立卡并改成卡号,缺了就判 REWORK;`l1-face` 也标了这一项。我在 head 上核过,欠的内容属实:`skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md:112` 写的是 `trackHistory` 默认 `false`、「Field-level audit trail」,本 PR 之后字段不写就是开着;`:104` 的 `enable` 一行也没有 `fieldHistory`。我在仓库里按 `fieldHistory skills` 搜了今天新开的卡,没有找到。立卡由席位来做;卡号回来后,请 dev 把 PR 正文这一行改掉(changeset 里没有这一行,不用加)。只改文字,我做增量审核时只核这一行。

## 席位核对(本轮已读,增量时不重读)

- 形态:`l1-face --pr 36399` 只标了 skills-docs 一项,也就是上面那一项。draft、base `main`、`Part of #36290`:这是 3 个 PR 里的第 1 个,所以用 `Part of` 是对的,卡要保留 `pm:dispatched`;卡上验收要求的截图归第 2、3 个 PR。88 个文件 +650 −107;`check-governed-merges` 判定 NOT governed。dogfood:没有 `!`,也没有 `(narrowing)`,所以不欠;正文照样在 head 上全量跑了一轮,4175 条里 4107 过、0 失败。
- 声明:`Clause-②: yes (widening)` 属实:新增可选键 `ObjectCapabilities.fieldHistory`,没有 `.default()`,`object.test.ts` 钉住了解析后不会写出这个键。`Metadata-protocol: semantic` 属实:是默认值变了,而且带了升级说明。按 ruling A,`semantic` 不算破坏性变更,所以不欠 ADR-0087 条目(`check-adr-0087-registration` 已过)。changeset 里 spec 和 plugin-audit 是 `minor`,其余 7 个包只是对象文件加了一个键,用 `patch`。
- 写入侧(`audit-writers.ts`):`changeValuesShownFor` 的判断顺序是:对象写了 `fieldHistory: false` 就全关;字段写了 `trackHistory: false`,或者字段属于 `collectMaskedReadFields` 收出来的凭据字段,就关;字段写了 `trackHistory: true` 就开;剩下的按类型判断,14 种媒体或结构化类型默认关,其余默认开。对象上的 `enable.trackHistory` 不参与这个判断,和 changeset 的说法一致。查关联记录标题的计划和渲染摘要读的是同一个判断。存储的摘要用 `fitStoredChangeSummary` 截到 `activitySummaryMaxLength()`:先把每一侧截到 60 字,再从后面去掉若干条改动,补上 `; …`;编码里的每一侧最多 1000 字。
- 读取侧(安全上最要紧的一段):`redactActivityRows` 对 `fieldChanges` 编码逐条判断:字段不在这个读者能读的集合里就去掉;关联字段要读者能拿到被引用记录的标题才保留。读不懂的 `fieldChanges` 编码直接删掉(读不懂就不给)。全部去掉时连编码一起删;摘要整条不可给但编码还剩几条时,用剩下的几条重新拼一句,不整条丢。其他编码仍然对非系统读者剥掉,`text_sources` 照旧剥掉。中间件的注册顺序换了:语言中间件在外,脱敏在内,所以按读者语言重拼摘要时用的是已经收窄的编码,不会用存储的完整编码。我按这个顺序把几种情况都推了一遍:被删掉的摘要不会被重新拼出来;非 `fieldChanges` 编码先按来源判断,再照原样剥掉。没有找到会漏出去的路径。
- 文本逐句核:changeset 的五条加最后一句都与 diff 一致。手写文档 `security.mdx` §7、`objects.mdx` 的开关表、`fields.mdx` 和 `validation-rules.mdx` 的 `trackHistory` 一行、两处 describe,都与 `changeValuesShownFor` 一致。生成的 `references/*` 与 describe 逐字相同。11 个语言的表单翻译包只加了 `fieldHistory` 的标签,并改了两句已经不对的 `trackHistory` 帮助文字。
- nit:三张文档表格里 `trackHistory` 那一行写的是「on unless the field or object turns them off」,没提媒体和 JSON 类字段默认关(`security.mdx` 和 describe 里提了),以后顺手补上即可,不改判。
- 测试证据:写入侧新增 8 条:不写就开;对象写 `false` 只记标签;只写 `enable.trackHistory: false` 照样开;字段写 `false` 只记标签;凭据字段只记标签;`json` 要写 `true` 才开;长文本能写进 500 以内,编码每侧截到 1000 并带 `…`;30 条改动能装下并带 `; …`。读取侧新增 6 条:系统读者拿到完整编码;被遮蔽的读者的编码里没有那个字段;读不到某字段的读者,编码和重拼的摘要里都没有它;对照读者拿到全部;非 `fieldChanges` 编码仍不给;关联字段按标题规则。消融:去掉逐条收窄的两个过滤,9/40 挂;去掉 `fieldHistory === false` 那一支,8/139 挂。我没有在本地重跑,读的是报告和 CI。
- 「随默认值一起动的文件」逐条有理由:两个 dogfood 用例里,`website` 没有写 `trackHistory`,现在会记值;`REF_TITLED` 加了 `fieldHistory: false`,好让那组「标题给不给」的用例仍然在测东西,不是空过。清单条目 rev 16、两处计数钉也写清了为什么动。
- CI @ `851997e6`:62 success · 12 expected skip · 0 failed · 0 pending;mergeable_state clean。
- 落地条款:非受管;这一项改完后做增量 L1,加上席位的 schema 面 L2;之后由区 ready + auto-merge;`Part of` ⇒ 卡保留 `pm:dispatched`。

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `851997e677adc14a324b8634a1325e683d58b11a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.form.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/activity-field-redaction.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/activity-summary-message.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

Inputs read: card #36290 with its four comments (triage, ruling 7076513167, claim 7076544277, dev report 7078070848), the PR #36399 body and its 87 files, the net diff from merge base `c448c6151d` to the head, and the check-runs on the head. Every check-run on the head is `success` or `skipped`, both `Check Changeset` runs included. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- New key `ObjectCapabilities.fieldHistory`, `z.boolean().optional()`, no default. This widens the accept set. Right. The no-default reason holds in the tree: `trackHistory` beside it is `.default(false)`, so a parsed `enable` block cannot tell an authored `false` from silence, and a new key without a default can.
- Field `trackHistory` keeps its schema (`z.boolean().optional()`). Its meaning changes: absent now shows values, where before only `true` did. Nothing is refused. This is a changed default, so `semantic`. Right.
- `enable.trackHistory` keeps its schema, its default and its readers (`api-derivation.ts`, the record page ledger gate). Only its describe moved. Right. The writer never read the object flag before either, so no object that wrote `trackHistory: false` loses a behaviour it had.
- Narrowing check, value by value. Field `trackHistory: false` reads as before (label only). Field `trackHistory: true` reads as before, with two exceptions. On a credential field it now gives the label only, where before it gave mask to mask: no information is lost. Under an object that writes the new `fieldHistory: false` it is off: no earlier author could have written that key. No value an author could write before is refused. I find no narrowing. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right.
- Wire surface. `metadata.summary_message` with key `fieldChanges` is now served to non-system readers, narrowed change by change. Every other code is still stripped. A reader not served the stored summary now gets a summary rebuilt from the kept changes, where before the column was dropped. Both widen. Right, and ruling point 2 asks for it.
- Wire surface, changed meaning. On an update with no opted-in field the stored summary used to name the record ("Updated Customer X: Notes"). It now reads "Notes: old value, new value" and names no record. `record_label` still carries the label. This follows from the ruling and is covered by `semantic`.
- Stored code values are capped at 1,000 characters a side, and the stored summary is fitted to 500. Before, an over-long tracked summary failed the insert on a SQL driver. `metadata.old` and `metadata.new` keep the whole value. Not a narrowing of anything an author writes.
- The values in the summary and the code come from the same masked ledger views that already fill `metadata.old` and `metadata.new`. So default-on adds no new class of value to the row. The only added content is referenced-record titles, and those pass the existing per-reader title rule.

### ② Semver level

- `Metadata-protocol: semantic` is right. The diff holds one `added` (the new key) and one `semantic` (the changed default). The rule ranks `semantic` over `added`, and nothing is `narrowed`.
- Levels match. `@objectstack/spec` minor and `@objectstack/plugin-audit` minor carry the kind. The seven packages that only add `fieldHistory: false` to their own objects take patch. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is on the PR body and in the changeset body, and it is right (see ①).
- Migration entry under the gate: none is owed. No key is removed, renamed or refused, and the registration gate treats a changed default as not breaking. The changeset states the upgrade step in words. A stored-row conversion is a separate question, and M1 raises it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, UI producers left to PR 2 (`FieldDesigner.tsx`, `ObjectFieldInspector.tsx`, a `fieldHistory` toggle in `ObjectSettingsPanel`). Not answered by a later PR alone. See M1.
- Dev flag, `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` still teaches `trackHistory` as the switch. Declared on the PR body as `Skills-docs: follow-up owed`. Accepted as a follow-up for the seat.
- The ruling reverses ADR-0052 §5b.1. The ADR text is not amended in this diff. The ruling names card #36086 as the carrier. Accepted on that carrier.
- The PR body says "PR 1 of 3". The claim says only "split into PRs". No effect on this head.
- SQL push-down: no new in-app join and no new id materialisation. The referenced-title read is the existing one, batched per target object. It now runs for every changed reference field, where before it ran only for opted-in fields. The cost per write is one read per target object. No finding.
- Security floor (ruling point 3): held in the code read. A change of a field the reader is not served is dropped from the code before the summary is rebuilt. A reference change is kept only under the title rule. A redaction failure strips `metadata` whole, so the code goes with it. Filters on the stored text stay refused for a withheld reader by the existing query guard. No security finding.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`

M1 (must-fix) — The new contract reads a stored field `trackHistory: false` as the author's choice to turn values off. The repository's own field designer writes that value for every field it saves. `ui/packages/plugin-designer/src/FieldDesigner.tsx` sets `trackHistory: data.trackHistory === true` on create and on edit, and `MetadataFieldsPage.tsx` (`fromDesignerField`) persists it as written. Until this head, `false` and absent meant the same thing to every reader, so that `false` was noise. From this head it is an opt-out. Three consequences follow. First, fields already saved through the designer stay label-only after the upgrade. That is the card's own scene, a self-built app, and ruling point 1 says values show by default on every object. Second, the PR body's line that stored objects take effect on upgrade with no rebuild is not true for those fields. Third, PR 2 as described only stops the producer from writing `false`. It does not touch stored definitions, and between this merge and PR 2 every designer save opts a field out without the author asking. Once a release ships this meaning, a stored `false` from the designer can no longer be told from a chosen one. The PR gives exactly this argument for `enable.fieldHistory` having no default, and then does not apply it to the field key. So this head does not stand on its own. One of these closes it: (a) an ADR-0087 stored-row conversion that drops a field's `trackHistory: false` written before this release, shipped in the same release as the flip, with the producer fix in the same PR or landed first; or (b) a maintainer ruling that designer-saved `false` stays off, quoted on the PR. Limit of this finding: I read the producer and the page code. I did not run the designer.

`packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts` and `packages/spec/src/data/field.form.ts`

S1 (should-fix) — The object form adds `{ field: 'fieldHistory', type: 'boolean' }` with no help text. Its label is "Field History" and it sits next to "Track History". For this key, absent means on, and `false` is the only value an author has a reason to write. A bare checkbox shows absent as unchecked, which reads as off. The field form has the same shape for `trackHistory`: its help text now says "on unless turned off", but a two-state control cannot show absent apart from `false`. Give the object row a help text that says what unchecked and untouched each mean, and make sure the form does not write `false` for a box the author never touched. If the renderer cannot hold a third state, say so on the PR and name the PR that carries it. I did not read the form renderer, so the write behaviour is unverified.

`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`

- The `fieldHistory` schema line, its jsdoc and the `trackHistory` describe agree with the writer, sentence by sentence. `changeValuesShownFor` returns off for `enable.fieldHistory === false`, does not read `enable.trackHistory`, and treats absent as on. The spec test pins that a parsed `enable` block carries no `fieldHistory` key. Holds.
- Nit: the field describe does not say that an explicit field `true` is still off under an object `fieldHistory: false`. The object describe covers it ("off for this object").

Implementing files

- `audit-writers.ts`: agrees with both describes. Credential fields come from `collectMaskedReadFields`, the engine's own predicate, not a second list. The fourteen no-line types are all members of `FieldType`. The fit to 500 cuts each side to 60 first, then drops trailing changes, then cuts the sentence, and the code keeps every change. Holds.
- Nit: `tree` is not in the reference set, so its change shows a stored id. Multi-value option types show stored values joined by commas, not labels. The card's acceptance names select, lookup and user only, and those three resolve.
- `activity-field-redaction.ts`: the code is narrowed by the same served set as `old` and `new`. A code with key `fieldChanges` that this version cannot read is deleted, which fails closed. The rebuilt summary uses the kept changes only. When the security service gives no answer, the row is left as it is, code included. That is the existing rule for `old`, `new` and the summary, and the code holds nothing those do not. Holds.
- `activity-summary-message.ts` and `audit-plugin.ts`: the order flip is sound. The redaction now runs first on the result. The summary middleware composes only when the `summary` key is still on the row, so a summary the redaction dropped is not rebuilt from a code. It still strips every code other than `fieldChanges` for a non-system reader. The two projection helpers do not remove each other's added columns. Holds.

Summary: the server half is correct and the declarations are right. The head fails on M1, a stored value whose meaning this PR changes while an in-repo producer still writes it.
